prompt_instruction: Audit free-neutron decay. Mark every account, then decide whether nature allows it.
explanation_formal: Every account balances, and the neutron is heavier than the proton plus the electron, so the decay is allowed. The antineutrino is what makes the lepton account close: the electron brings Lₑ = +1 and the antineutrino −1.
explanation_intuitive: The books balance: the electron’s +1 on the electron sub-account is cancelled by the antineutrino’s −1, and there are three half-integer spins out for the neutron’s one in.
explanation_steps: Baryon number: n has B = 1 (udd, three × ⅓); p has B = 1 (uud). Balances.
Lepton number: 0 → (e⁻: +1) + (ν̄ₑ: −1) = 0, and the same for Lₑ. L_μ and L_τ are 0 throughout.
Half-integer spins: 1 in, 3 out. Both odd, so the necessary condition holds.
Threshold: m(n) − m(p) − m(e) ≈ 939.565 − 938.272 − 0.511 = 0.782 MeV > 0. Allowed, with very little to spare.
A neutrino appears, so the force is weak.
source: PDG 2026 masses (n, p, e⁻); spec §6 golden case

prompt_instruction: Someone proposes that the neutron decays to a proton and an electron only. Audit it.
explanation_formal: Charge and baryon number balance, and there is energy to spare, but lepton number goes from 0 to 1 and the half-integer-spin count goes from one to two. Two independent accounts fail.
explanation_intuitive: Without the antineutrino the lepton count gains a unit from nowhere, and a single spin-½ particle cannot turn into two: half-integers only pair up.
explanation_steps: Lepton number: 0 → +1 (the electron). Violated, and so is the electron sub-account Lₑ.
Half-integer spins: 1 in, 2 out. One odd, one even: two spin-½ particles combine to integer spin, which cannot equal the neutron’s ½. Violated.
Historically, this missing energy and spin was why Pauli proposed the neutrino.
source: Spec §6 golden case; historical note from Griffiths 2e (chapter to be confirmed)

register_tags.intuitive: Can the Proton Close Its Account?

prompt_instruction: Grand unified theories predict this decay. Audit it with the Standard Model ledger.
explanation_formal: Charge balances and the energy is there, but baryon number goes from 1 to 0 and lepton number from 0 to −1. Their difference, B − L, is conserved (1 → 1). The Standard Model forbids the decay; experiments find τ(p → e⁺π⁰) > 2.4 × 10³⁴ years.
explanation_intuitive: The quark count drops by one and the lepton count drops by one at the same time. The two errors cancel in B − L, but each account is broken on its own.
explanation_steps: Baryon number: 1 → 0 (the positron and the pion carry none). Violated.
Lepton number: 0 → −1 (e⁺ is an antilepton). Violated, and so is Lₑ.
B − L: 1 − 0 = 1 before, 0 − (−1) = 1 after. Conserved, as grand unified theories typically keep it.
Threshold: 938.3 MeV > 0.5 + 135.0 MeV, so energy is not the obstacle.
source: PDG 2026, Tests of Conservation Laws §6 (B − L, proton lifetime limit)
